Posterior phase contrast on the response scale

Source: R/utils-posterior-decisions.R
compute_phase_contrast.Rd

Computes the posterior distribution of an end-of-phase contrast (e.g., phase B vs phase A) on the outcome's response scale using brms::posterior_epred. Supported for families with a scalar mean on the response scale (gaussian, student, skew_normal, poisson, negbinomial, zero_inflated_poisson, bernoulli, beta, Gamma). Ordinal and categorical families (cumulative, sratio, cratio, acat, categorical) are not supported, since a response-scale mean contrast is not well defined for them; read those effects on the link scale via summarize_fixed_effect_decisions(). Designs with more than two phases (alternating-treatment, changing-criterion) require explicit from/to labels.

Usage

compute_phase_contrast(
  model,
  data = NULL,
  from = "A",
  to = "B",
  phase_var = "phase",
  case_var = "case",
  time_var = "time",
  at_session = c("last", "mean"),
  per_case = TRUE,
  threshold = NULL,
  rope = NULL,
  intervention_goal = c("increase", "decrease"),
  ci_level = 0.95
)

Arguments

model

A fitted brmsfit.

data

Data frame; defaults to model$data.

from

Character. Reference phase for the baseline side of the contrast (default "A").

to

Character. Reference phase for the treatment side of the contrast (default "B").

phase_var

Name of the phase column (default "phase").

case_var

Name of the case column (default "case").

time_var

Name of the time column (default "time").

at_session

"last" (last session of each phase, default) or "mean" (average across all sessions of each phase).

per_case

Logical; include per-case contrasts (default TRUE).

threshold

Numeric. A positive magnitude on the improvement-oriented scale (i.e., after any decrease reflection). If supplied, posterior probability that the contrast meets or exceeds this clinically meaningful change is reported as prob_meaningful_change.

rope

Numeric length-2. ROPE bounds on the response scale. For intervention_goal = "decrease" the bounds are reflected together with the contrast, so an asymmetric ROPE stays attached to the same region. If supplied, posterior probability inside the ROPE is reported as rope_prob.

intervention_goal

"increase" (default) or "decrease". When "decrease", the contrast sign is flipped so positive values denote improvement, and the ROPE is reflected with it.

ci_level

Credible interval width (default 0.95).

Value

A list with:

population_contrast

One-row data frame: posterior mean, SD, lower / upper credible bounds, probability of direction, optional prob_meaningful_change and rope_prob.

per_case_contrast

Data frame of per-case contrasts with the same columns plus case. NULL if per_case = FALSE.

draws

Numeric vector of posterior draws for the population contrast.

metadata

Arguments recorded for downstream reporting.

Details

Reference rows are drawn from the fitted data. With at_session = "last", the last session per case in each phase is used; with at_session = "mean", all sessions in each phase contribute and are averaged per draw.

The population contrast is a typical-case contrast of observed rows: it predicts with re_formula = NA (every random effect at zero) and compares rows from the two phases, which sit at different sessions. On a nonlinear link, the expected outcome at zero random effects is not the population average, and the two sides differ in time as well as condition. marginal_contrast() gives the population-averaged contrast at one common session, averaging over new cases drawn from the random-effect distribution with and without treatment. The per-case contrasts include each case's random effects.

Examples

if (interactive()) {
  dat <- simulate_scd_data()
  fit <- brms::brm(outcome ~ phase + (1 | case), data = dat, refresh = 0)
  compute_phase_contrast(fit, threshold = 5, rope = c(-1, 1))
}
